title: Which sums can never come from these two dice?
description: Two dice with the same six faces are rolled and the top numbers are added. The sums are sorted into three kinds, two negative faces, two positive faces, and one of each, and the numbers from minus ten to twelve that never appear are found. The video breaks the slip of thinking that every number between the smallest and the largest sum can be rolled.
teaching_notes: One idea: sort the sums by the signs of the two faces, list each kind, then see which numbers in the range are left out. Watch for students who think every number between the smallest and the largest sum can be rolled.

video_script.why: The child adds every pair of faces by the sign rules and sees that some integers in the range are never reached.
video_script.substitution: The book's two dice with faces −1, 2, −3, 4, −5, 6, sorted by the signs of the two faces rolled.
video_script.anchor: the two dice of the book, each with the faces −1, 2, −3, 4, −5 and 6
video_script.payoff_line: Eight numbers between minus ten and twelve can never be the sum

final_answer.spoken: minus nine, minus seven, minus five, zero, two, seven, nine and eleven

never_show: the list of missing numbers before the answer
maths_rules: numbers from −10 to 12: 10 negative + zero + 12 positive = 23
video_script.design: One pair of dice drawn at the top, three rows of sums built below it, and one strip of the numbers from minus ten to twelve that collects ticks.

<bookmark mark='ask'/>The largest sum is twelve. Which numbers in between can never be the sum?
